title: postfix ! in a call argument compiles and runs, which is the commonest shape in the language
notes: RETIRED REFUSAL, kept under its old filename so the COVERAGE.md row that cites it (§4.16) keeps resolving. specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the placement walk; see DECISIONS.md §Typed failures. WHY IT NOW PASSES, and this case is the one where the reason is worth spelling out: an argument is evaluated after the callee and after every argument to its left, so the hoist is order-preserving exactly when nothing to the left leaves an effect behind. Here the callee is the identifier `shout` and there is no earlier argument, so the emitted program calls `lookup`, checks, then calls `shout` — the authored order. The condition that survives is `precededByUnhoistedEffect` in poc/src/language/semantic.ts, which still refuses `g() + r!`; a call argument as such is not refused by anything.
